neighbours.label: the start of a scheduled run or an era: ' season' as the object of opens / kicks off / launches (a team's or company's season), and ' begins' / ' starts' / ' began' in 'modern X begins with …'; not ' season' as weather, produce or 'last season'
fire: The ballet company opens its season with Giselle next week.
The Tigers kick off their season at home against Boston on Saturday.
Modern antitrust law begins with this famous ruling from 1911.
The women's soccer team was kicking off its season in Ohio.
The theatre launches its season with a new comedy in October.
The modern labor movement began with the strikes of the 1880s.
The opera house opens its season on Friday with Tosca.
The history of modern surgery starts with the discovery of anesthesia.
quiet: The ballet company will rehearse Giselle in the old hall next week.
The Tigers lost at home against Boston on Saturday.
The dry season lasts from May to October in the north.
The women's soccer team was travelling by bus through Ohio.
The theatre sells cheap tickets for students in October.
Strawberries are in season and cheap at the market in June.
He scored twenty goals last season and won the award.
The surgeon finished the operation and went home to rest.

notes: Card: ' season' x4, ' led' x3, ' begins' x2; output promotes ' starting', ' first', ' begin', ' starts'. Probes: 'opens its season' 0.92, 'kicks off its season' 0.56, 'begins with this discovery' 0.45, 'starts with Lavoisier' 0.38, 'movement began' 0.20; 'rainy season' 0.03, 'last season' 0.04. Caveat seen in probing: 'closes its season' 0.51 and 'ended its season' 0.24, so the ' season' part is about a run being opened or closed rather than only beginnings; the near misses here use weather/produce/'last season' and season-free sports lines.
